{"id":"mimid-1wgh.46.11.2","title":"coland interop: peer auth is RFC 9421 HTTP signatures with DID keys, not mutual TLS (-07 §4 MUST)","description":"Side: coland (deviation from the draft MUST).

protocol-06/-07 §4 (-07 txt line ~981): "The TLS connection underlying the HTTPS connection MUST be mutually authenticated", with certificates that authenticate the source and target provider domains. coland's facade does not use TLS client certificates at all. Every MIMI operation except the directory requires RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures, scenario ak.http_signature.scenario.mimi_provider.v1, label sig1, covering content-digest, source-service-id, destination-service-id and provider-id (plus mimi-room-uri, idempotency-key and the trust-domain headers when they apply). The required headers are Signature, Signature-Input, Arkret-Operation, Content-Digest, Source-Service-ID (an Arkret DID core id, for example ak:did_core:key:z6Mk... or ak:did_core:web:host), Destination-Service-ID (= coland's ak:did_core:webvh:Qmbt1KN87RzzrzXEvtceNq35pfvcDtaDBGW7zBs5MiQqux) and Provider-ID (mimi://...). The keyid must be a DID URL whose controller projects to Source-Service-ID. The key is resolved via did:key (offline), did:web or did:webvh (HTTPS fetch), or a configured federation peer. There is no CA trust list or provider allowlist, only optional denylists.
- Verified live: unsigned POST gives 401 http_signature_required. A did:key-signed identifiers/query from an unregistered source is accepted (probe in scratchpad coland/probe).
- Impact: mimid cannot call any coland MIMI operation, because it has no HTTP-signature signer and no DID. Its mTLS client cert (interop CA 9C:22:...:C2) is irrelevant to coland, and coland cannot verify it.
Code: crates/http/src/routing/interop/mimi/signature.rs; arkret-spec spec/v1/zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §5 (the list of signed operations).
